articles.title: Magical Realist Tale ‘6TM’ and ‘Searching for SmarterChild,’ About One of the Earliest Chatbots, Win Top Industry Awards at Ji.hlava Festival
articles.summary: “6TM,” directed by Karim Akalay and produced by Walid Bekhti, won the New Visions Award for the most promising European project at the Ji.hlava Documentary Film Festival on Friday.
body: The jury said, “With its imaginative blend of magical realism, humor and social relevance, ‘6TM ‘ offers a fresh vision of European cinema. Rooted in lived experience and shaped through co-creation, ‘6TM’ challenges conventional representations and opens up new possibilities for who gets to tell stories, whose voices are heard, and who sees themselves reflected on screen. We believe this approach holds extraordinary promise for the next generation of both audiences and filmmakers, demonstrating how cinema can become more inclusive and participatory.”

The jury was composed of Katrine Kiilgaard, managing director of CPH:DOX in Denmark; Anda Ionescu, managing partner and producer at Tangaj Production in Romania; and Robert Y. Chang, co-producer of American Documentary at POV in the U.S.

The award was presented in cooperation with UPP, which donated an in-kind grant for visual post-production worth about 15,000 Euros, and Soundaquare, which provided sound mixing and a final sound master, with an estimated value of 5,000 Euros.

articles.title: Marvin R. Shanken, Longtime Publisher and Editor of Wine Spectator, Dies at 83
articles.summary: Marvin R. Shanken, the longtime editor and publisher of Wine Spectator magazine who was instrumental in elevating the profile of American wine business, died Thursday in Manhattan. He was 83.
body: Wine Spectator became a key educational tool to help consumers become more familiar with the beverage, and contributed significantly to raising the status of the Napa Valley wine region. Wine Spectator articles utilized the 100 point wine rating system, which made buying fine bottles much more approachable for the general audience.

Shanken also founded the magazine Cigar Aficionado and purchased Food Arts and Malt Advocate, which was renamed Whisky Advocate. Other publications he founded through his M. Shanken Communications include Market Watch and Shanken News Daily.

“He helped educate millions of Americans on the joys and virtues of wine, and tirelessly encouraged and pushed winemakers to produce the best for their customers,” Wine Spectator wrote in its obituary.

Among his many milestones were establishing Wine Spectator’s Restaurant Awards program, taking over the long-running Wine Experience weekend to bring producers together with consumers and creating the Wine Spectator Scholarship Foundation.

articles.title: Cate Blanchett-Backed Group and Collection of Hollywood Stars File Brief in New York Times-OpenAI Lawsuit: Hollywood Has ‘Proven Infrastructure’ to License Content
articles.summary: The Human Consent Foundation, the Cate Blanchett-backed nonprofit trying to protect the likenesses of individuals from unauthorized scraping by AI models, and a legion of Hollywood companies have filed an amicus brief in the New York Times’ lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming the tech…
body: “Defendants have argued that licensing creative works for AI training is cost-prohibitive,” the brief read. “Defendants also claim there is no settled means of valuing training data. The facts demonstrate otherwise. The creative industries already have in place a proven infrastructure and workflows to clear rights for dispersed works at scale and cost-effectively.”

In a statement, HCF co-founder and CEO Nikki Hexum said the filing was intended to show the court “how the creative industry actually works and acknowledge the solutions that have been built and are continuing to develop for this new digital era.”

“Our goal is to ensure that as the market for AI data licensing grows, the humans who create the value in that market are protected and have a meaningful choice,” Hexum added. “We are not starting from scratch. There is already a functioning market and infrastructure for licensing creative work. We just need to ensure that new AI technology respects those boundaries and choices, including the choice not to participate.”

articles.title: ‘Obsession’ Director Curry Barker Pitched Nathan Fielder a Collaboration After Watching ‘You Can See Everything’: ‘I Put It Out in the Water’
articles.summary: “Obsession” director Curry Barker is not only a fan of “You Can See Everything,” but he’s already reached out to Nathan Fielder about working together. “I thought it was freakin’ insane and awesome,” Barker told Variety Thursday night at the Time100 Next Gala at Pier59 Studios.
body: When asked about potentially collaborating with Fielder, the “Obsession” director revealed he’s already floated the idea to him: “I told him that. I said, ‘Hey!’ … I just put it out in the water.”

“You Can See Everything” blurs the line between narrative and documentary storytelling and, as Variety’s chief awards editor Clayton Davis puts it, has “turned the movie landscape topsy-turvy.” Much like Barker’s “Obsession,” the film has left the industry re-examining what kinds of movies resonate with Gen Z audiences — and, more importantly, what drives them out to the theaters.
“It felt new, fresh, different,” Barker said of “You Can See Everything.” “You almost can’t even call it a documentary, but it totally is. I’m just a huge fan of what [Fielder] is doing.”
Barker should have plenty more chances to cross paths with Fielder on the awards circuit, as both their films continue to earn recognition alongside some of the year’s most acclaimed films.

articles.title: Celebrity Traitors comes to a climax in nail-biting final
articles.summary: The second series of the hit series reached its climax on Friday after attracting 15 million viewers.
body: We've had four weeks of suspense, suspicion and very suspect tactics, as some of Britain's biggest stars engaged in a battle of wits to win the most popular show on TV.
The second series of BBC One's The Celebrity Traitors reached its climax on Friday, with the 21 original contestants having been reduced to seven before the final.
They were then whittled down to two winners - with the faithful duo of comedian Romesh Ranganathan and Heartstopper actor Sebastian "Bash" Croft emerging victorious.
The players successfully banished the remaining traitors - Love Island host Maya Jama and YouTuber King Kenny - in dramatic fashion, and the winning pair shared the £83,000 prize for their charities.

articles.title: How Bristol shaped Maya Jama before her TV fame
articles.summary: The Love Island host's journey from leaving Bristol as a teenager to reaching the BBC show's finale.
body: Maya Jama has gone from Bristol schoolgirl to one of the UK's biggest television stars.
The 32-year-old Love Island host was watched by millions as she faced the last round table in the final of The Celebrity Traitors, which aired on BBC One and iPlayer.
But behind the glamorous television appearances and red carpet moments is a story that began in a council house with a young girl determined to make it on the small screen.
Maya was born and raised in Bristol, growing up in St Paul's with a family of Bristol Rovers supporters, putting on song and dance performances for them and charging 20p a time.

articles.title: Party Rock Anthem singer struggled with mental health before death
articles.summary: Lauren Bennett, who featured on LMFAO's hit song, was found dead by her husband.
body: A British singer who was a member of the girl group G.R.L took her own life, an inquest has found.
Lauren Bennett, 36, who also featured on LMFAO's 2011 hit Party Rock Anthem, was found dead in Kent on 29 May.
In a statement read out by an assistant coroner on Friday, her husband Kenny Wormald said she had been struggling with severe mental health issues before her death.
The court heard she told him she was going out for a walk on the morning of her death while he remained in bed half asleep.

articles.title: Sir Patrick Stewart remembered as 'Mirfield's finest'
articles.summary: Tributes have been paid to the legendary Star Trek actor Sir Patrick Stewart, who was born in Mirfield.
body: Sir Patrick Stewart once said he had to drop his Yorkshire accent for Hollywood, but he never forgot his roots.

The Mirfield-born actor, best known for his roles in Star Trek and the X-Men films, died at the age of 86 at his home in Los Angeles on Wednesday after suffering with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.
His death has prompted an outpouring of love from the community he proudly called home, along with his beloved Huddersfield Town - the club he followed from childhood.
Stewart's friend and fellow legendary actor Sir Ian McKellen said Stewart "never forsook his origins".

articles.title: Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards
articles.summary: Generational hitmaker Desmond Child and Kobalt CEO Laurent Hubert were also recognized at the ceremony, held at the Skirball Cultural Center.
body: The Songwriters of North America honored Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, Desmond Child, the songwriters behind KPop Demon Hunters and Kobalt Music CEO Laurent Hubert at the organization’s annual awards show at Los Angeles’ Skirball Cultural Center on Thursday, in a night that celebrated the industry’s under-appreciated hitmakers while rallying the business on music’s most pressing issues from censorship to copyright law and the rise of AI.

“Joe Hill’s union anthems put wind in the sails of those fighting for an eight-hour work day. ‘We Shall Overcome’ steeled the resolve of freedom fighters during the civil rights movement. Jimi Hendrix’s ‘Star-Spangled Banner’ channeled the moral cacophony of the Vietnam War through a Marshall Stack. And one or two Rage Against The Machine songs were heard pumping in the streets of Brazil after Lula defeated that fascist prick the other day,” Morello said, referring to defeated former Brazil president Jair Bolsonaro.

articles.title: 5 Best New Movies And Shows To Stream This Weekend On Netflix, HBO Max, Paramount Plus And More (Oct. 30-Nov. 1)
articles.summary: If you want something brand new to watch over Halloween weekend, we've got you covered. These recommendations encompass offerings from multiple streamers.
body: Can you believe October is over already? I know I can't. With October just about in the rearview mirror and the final weekend happening over Halloween, plenty of people are probably planning their Elizabeth Holmes-inspired get-ups or figuring out how to perfectly drape some old sheets to approximate the period costumes from "The Odyssey." If you're a homebody looking to stream some good stuff over the weekend, though, we've got you covered with some solid picks.

Everything on this list is either completely new and exclusive to one streaming network or the premiere of a new theatrical hit coming to streaming for the first time, so just because your favorite movie got randomly added to Netflix, Hulu, or HBO Max doesn't mean it will make the cut here. From a truly stunning documentary series about a star we lost too soon to two major season premieres to an animated movie that's actually fun for the whole family, here are five movies and TV shows you should watch on major streamers this weekend, October 30 to November 1, 2026.
